notes.title: Fuchian Chronicles - The Last Fox Fighter Now Available!
notes.content:
Hello everyone, hope you’re all enjoying the holiday season! I come bearing gifts, in the form of the Last Fox Fighter!

[previewyoutube=-M4gjy23vYI;full][/previewyoutube]

Yes, The Last Fox Fighter is now available for free for all owners of Fuchian Chronicles (which is 25% off as part of the Steam 2024 Winter Sale!). Simply go to the DLC page and add it to your library, and you’ll be able to pick whether to play Fuchian Chronicles or The Last Fox Fighter whenever you launch Fuchian Chronicles. The web-playable itch.io version will remain free to everyone regardless of whether or not you own Fuchian Chronicles, and the full version will be available for $1 there as well. I know I previously said I wouldn’t sell it, but I feel this is a decent way to give owners of Fuchian Chronicles an added bonus without alienating those who are only interested in The Last Fox Fighter. Thank you for understanding. Newly added features in the release version of The Last Fox Fighter include:


 A short story consisting of 9 stages
 Two ground levels
 Stage select and free play option upon story completion
 Databank with descriptions of enemies and their behavior
 New enemies: bunnoid missile and defence platform


There were also a number of tweaks, including:


 New weapon effects as you level up your weapons’ damage
 New visual effects for RCS thrusters and boost ability
 Stage transition now requires a button press instead of happening as soon as you touch it
 Turrets and some enemies now lead their shots, making it harder to dodge
 Balance changes, such as number of shots fired at once, faster resource gain, and bigger play area for some stages
 Additional settings, including one to change the maximum number of enemies allowed at once, which can improve performance if the game starts to lag


If you find any bugs please post it in the bug reporting thread in the Steam community, or if you prefer, email me directly at shentzugames@yahoo.com. I’ll fix them and push an update as soon as I’m able.

Finally, as I said in my previous announcement, I will be stepping away from game development for the foreseeable future. Thank you for all your support. I still love making games and fully intend to come back to it in the future, including making a sequel to Fuchian Chronicles. I just need to get things in order first. I still plan on doing some game jams when I can, so please follow my bluesky for updates!

Merry Christmas and Happy Holidays,
- ShenTzu

notes.title: An Update
notes.content:
Hey there, hope you’re all doing well! It’s been a while, hasn’t it? I’ve been busy trying out and learning different game engines to use for my next game. After trying out GameMaker2 and Unity, I eventually decided on Godot and am in the process of making a small game with it. What game you ask? A top down twin-stick shooter set in the Fuchian Chronicles universe!

https://i.imgur.com/6Q55VUN.gif

The Last Fox Fighter (working title) is still in its prototype stages and I’m still figuring out how to add the features that I want, but I’ve made good progress in the 2-3 weeks I’ve spent on it! Normally I’d list out what’s in the prototype right now here, but you can see for yourself. The prototype is publicly available on its itch.io page, and you can play it in your browser! I update the game whenever I’ve added enough new features to justify an update, and feedback is always welcome!

I should be clear however, that I haven’t decided to make the Last Fox Fighter into a full game just yet. I’m still waiting to see how a few things pan out, and will continue to work on the prototype in the meantime. Once I’m satisfied with it, I’ll release the Last Fox Fighter as a free DLC for Fuchian Chronicles. If I do decide to make it into a full game, it will serve as a demo instead.

One final thing. If you follow me on Twitter/X, you may have noticed that my account has been suspended. The stated reason was that I violated a rule, but I don’t know what rule I violated and my best guess is that it’s because I often posted links to my Steam/itchio pages which might have been flagged as bot behaviour. So far I’ve only gotten one sentence automated responses saying they won’t help whenever I tried to appeal, so at this point I’ve written off the account as lost [strike]and have made a new one: @ShenTzuGame[/strike]. Nevermind, the new account got banned as well for ban evasion. Which, while understandable, is incredibly frustrating since I only made a new account because I wasn't able to appeal my old account. I'm trying to appeal again from the new account, and so far I haven't gotten an automated response yet so maybe there's hope. I'll edit again when there's a clear outcome.

I’m considering other platforms such as Mastadon or Bluesky as well, and will let you guys know if I make accounts there. Of course, you can still reach me here in the Steam Community or email me at shentzugames@yahoo.com. 

That’s it for this time, thanks for your time. I’ll post again when I have more to share, so look forward to that!

Sincerely,
ShenTzu

notes.title: Playtest Beta Now Available!
notes.content:
Hey everyone, hope you’re doing well! Turns out the previous announcement isn’t the last one before full release, but there’s a good reason for it! A playtest version of the final build of Fuchian Chronicles is now available for anyone who’d like to help me playtest one more time and catch any bugs that I’ve missed (or if you just want to play the final build early, that’s fine too!). It includes all the previously shown UI/walking animation updates, a brand new logo/main menu, expanded Databank, new portraits, and a few tweaked/expanded scenes. Aside from bug fixes and perhaps one or two more tweaks, this should be the final version of Fuchian Chronicles. I hope you like it!

https://i.imgur.com/nI6YF9d.gif

To access it, right click Fuchian Chronicles in your Steam Library, click “Properties”, click “Betas” on the left, and enter the code “foxesgokonkon”. That will unlock the “devtestbuild” with the playtest version of the final build and you’ll be able to play it. The main reason I went with an opt-in build instead of updating the main one is because the final release build requires you to start a new game due to some new functionality. If you’re in the middle of a run, feel free to finish that first if you don’t want to lose your progress. As always, please let me know about any bugs or issues you run into in the Steam Discussion thread, or email me at shentzugames@yahoo.com, which leads me to the last thing for this update.

Your feedback and help with playtesting has been a great help to me while Fuchian Chronicles is in Early Access. As such, I’d like to put everyone who has posted in the bug report and suggestions threads, and those who have sent me emails, in the game’s credits as playtesters for the final, final release. I don’t want to assume that everyone’s okay with it though, so this will be an opt-in thing. If you’d like to be added to the credits, please either reply to this announcement or email me at the address above.

That’s it for this update! With the bulk of development done, I’ll be working on updating the store page and marketing material such as screenshots and trailers from now till final release. Thank you once again for all your support thus far, and I hope you enjoy the final version of Fuchian Chronicles, whether you decide to play it now or at release on April 19th!

Sincerely,
- ShenTzu

notes.title: Pre-Release Update 3
notes.content:
Hello everyone, and welcome to what should be the final update prior to Fuchian Chronicle’s full release! This will be a text heavy one so please bear with me here.

I’ve fixed all the issues I mentioned in the previous updates, and addressed another one of the major complaints that I got:

[center]https://static.wixstatic.com/media/e4c1c1_adbdddf97f3741539435a5117b7b4a58~mv2.gif[/center]

New walking animations! This was an issue that was first brought up near the start of development, and I thought I had fixed it with a sprite update. The feedback I got however, made it clear that the lackluster animation hadn’t been adequately addressed. I hope that this new update goes further towards fixing that issue.

Now I’m back to adding new content to the game and playtesting to make sure everything is in order. I’ve already showed most of the new stuff I’m adding in the previous updates, but there is one thing I’m taking out: selectable battlemodes. The main reason for this is that the Action Time Battle (ATB) mode simply looks too unpolished, especially with how barebones the enemy ATB gauges looks and how it doesn’t line up with the enemy when the camera moves. If there’s one takeaway I got from all the feedback I got, it’s that looking unpolished is a big red flag. I’m fully aware that there are other parts of Fuchian Chronicles that look unpolished, but many of those cannot be feasibly fixed at this point. I can improve polish by removing ATB mode though, and so I’m doing that, and setting Conditional Turn Based (CTB) mode as the only battle mode. I don’t know how much being able to change battle modes affects your enjoyment of Fuchian Chronicles, but I hope you can see my reasoning and thank you for understanding.

The Steam store page is in need of serious overhaul as well. All the screenshots and trailers need replacing, I’ll need to rewrite the introduction blurb and some of the descriptions, and I’m even looking into getting a brand new logo for Fuchian Chronicles. I am taking new screenshots and recording clips as I playtest (and I’m sharing them on my Twitter/X @ShenTzuGames), but I’m in the slightly awkward position where Fuchian Chronicles is purchasable and playable while the new screenshots aren’t reflective of the current published version of the game. Because of this, I’ve decided to hold off on publishing any changes to the store page until final release so anyone who buys the game now will get what was advertised. As stated before, the price will not increase upon final release, but as a matter of disclosure, Fuchian Chronicles is part of the Steam Spring Sale, which will likely have a larger discount than the launch discount. If you’d like to hold off on buying/playing Fuchian Chronicles until final release, I’d completely understand and even encourage you to do so if you’re not satisfied with what you’ve seen in my updates.

So when is final release? Barring any major set-back or unforeseen circumstances, Fuchian Chronicles will come out of Early Access on April 19th, 2024! It’s been a long road, longer than I anticipated (but that’s how things are sometimes), and I thank you for your support thus far. I’m looking forward to finishing Fuchian Chronicles, and hope you will enjoy the game!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Pre-Release Update 2
notes.content:
Early update announcement this time for a few reasons. First, more art!

https://i.imgur.com/zfE8SwW.png

Getting art for all party members was one of my priorities in this final phase of development, and with Ferdi and Arlette’s portraits completed, that’s that part finished! Some of their dialogues have also been updated, namely their introductions. A handful of other recurring characters may get more art later, but there are more pressing matters at the moment.

If you’ve been following my social media (@ShenTzuGames on X/Twitter), you’ll know that I recently got a lot of feedback for Fuchian Chronicles. I’m extremely grateful for this, especially since they pointed out several major issues I had not considered. Unfortunately some of them simply can’t be feasibly fixed at this stage given my limited resources, but I am committed to improving what I can, starting with updating the UI.

https://i.imgur.com/stBXcVQ.png

https://i.imgur.com/d9jpWOE.jpeg

https://i.imgur.com/9cuxcwU.png

I will readily admit that I put too much focus on looking “unique” and overlooked player readability, and I hope you will agree that the updated UI is much cleaner than before. Additional fixes are in the works, and more feedback is always welcome! That said, these fixes likely won’t be implemented until final release, so I won’t be updating the screenshots and trailers on the Steam page at this point as to not give the wrong impression. Please follow my X/Twitter if you’d like to see the updates as they come. 

Finally and perhaps most importantly, the price of Fuchian Chronicle has been permanently reduced to $7.99 USD as of this announcement. I was under the impression that a cheap game would be seen as not worth considering, and overcorrected when I gave it a price tag of over $10 USD, especially considering the other amazing games you can get at that price. Just to be clear, $7.99 USD will be the final base price at release. If you previously bought Fuchian Chronicles at a higher price, I thank you for the support! I understand if you wish to refund the game though, and hope you’ll buy it again at the reduced price if you do. Fuchian Chronicles will also be part of the upcoming RPG Maker Franchise Sale and Steam Spring Sales (I can’t say when, but really soon!), so look forward to that!

That’s it for this time. I need to travel for two weeks starting next week, and combined with the need to fix the aforementioned issues, I’m currently predicting a final release date of sometime between early to mid-April. I’ll announce a concrete release date when I know one. As always, thank you for the continued support, and I hope you enjoy Fuchian Chronicles!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Pre-Release Update 1
notes.content:
First update after Fuchian Chronicles’ story officially concluded! If you follow my social media (@ShenTzuGames on X/Twitter, u/ShenTzuGames on Reddit), you’ll see that I’ve been much more active in posting stuff from the game. Now that development of the game proper is winding down, I have more time for these things and making more promotional material, so look forward to those!

That’s not to say there aren’t changes to the game in the works. For starters:

https://i.imgur.com/BxQDEPD.png

Character profiles! They’re mostly done now and I will be/have been sharing them over time on my X/Twitter. Not every named character will have one, but I did make one for most recurring characters, as well as a few of the important ones. That said… you may have noticed who the profile is of: Fitz! 

I originally didn’t have much planned for Fitz, and even planned to kill him off in Chapter 2 (hint: he can still die there depending on your actions!). But he got a bigger role as a development went on, and even became a temporary party member in certain points. With that in mind, I decided it was time he finally got his own portraits for all his appearances. I’ll also be expanding his introduction in Chapter 1 where he was basically another no-face NPC, and may expand his appearances in other chapters too.

Other parts of the game are slated for tweaking as well, one of them being increasing the number of autosave/quicksave slots from 1 to 3. That’s already finished, but I haven’t uploaded the change yet because IT WILL RENDER THE FIRST FOUR (4) SLOTS INACCESSIBLE. This means that if you have any manual saves in slots 1-4, THEY WILL BE OVERWRITTEN. So if you’re in the middle of the game, please make a manual save in one of the later save slots (slot 10 or higher to be safe). The plan is to publish this change when Fuchian Chronicles comes out of Early Access, but if you guys would like, I can publish this change earlier along with what I have finished. Let me know if that’s something you’d like, and I’ll make a small post warning you guys if I push the update early.

That’s it for this update! As always, please let me know if you encounter any bugs and I’ll fix them asap. I would also like to ask for another favour: please consider writing a review for Fuchian Chronicles! It would really help with the algorithm, and I’d love to hear your thoughts on the game, both positive and negative. Thank you once again for all your support, and I hope you like my game!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Chapter 7 now available!
notes.content:
Thank you for waiting, Chapter 7, the finale of Fuchian Chronicles, is finally here!

https://i.imgur.com/KyKWWl8.jpeg

After the events of Chapter 6, the future of the Empire is shrouded in uncertainty, but now a new operation is planned to end the war once and for all. Will it succeed? If so, at what cost? And what will it mean for Kimi and her crew?

In addition the new chapter, several things have been changed/balanced and a few bugs have been fixed. The demo has also been updated with these changes where appropriate. They are as follows:

-	The map in the ending scene of Chapter 5 has been redone for consistency
-	Healing items and skills now show approximately how much they restore in their description
-	The “Transfer Energy” ship skill now transfers 50 energy instead of 100.
-	Enemies are slightly harder to stun.
-	Fixed enemies dropping the wrong weapons when killed.
-	Settings for autosave interval and combat mode have been moved to the Options menu. The settings have been reset to the default (5 mins autosave interval and ATB combat), so please check the settings before you load your game!
-	Added “Quit Game” button to main menu (finally)
-	Added difficulty selector at the start of the game. You can still change it at any time in the settings!
-	Added a new joke game over to Chapter 1 with its own achievement

With the release of Chapter 7, Fuchian Chronicles is now story complete! However, that doesn’t mean the game is ready to come out of Early Access just yet. I would like to take some more time to give the game a once over, polishing up a few things and adding some extra content. Here are some of things I want to do in this phase:

-	Additional character portraits, such as for Fitz
-	Character profile entries in the encyclopaedia
-	Proper unlocking of encyclopaedia entries like in the demo
-	More CG

There are others, but these are the main things I’ll be working on. I will also be doing more work promoting the game during this time, so I may not get to all of them so I don’t want to overpromise and under deliver. Life as a solo developer isn’t easy after all. Either way, I’m planning on finishing and fully releasing Fuchian Chronicles in Q1 2024, and updates will come monthly as usual.

That’s it for this time, I hope you like the new chapter! As always, if you encounter any bugs please post them in the Steam Community thread or email me at shentzugames@yahoo.com. There’s no price increase this time (mainly so I can participate in sales), but there will be one final price increase when Fuchian Chronicles comes out of Early Access, so this is the best time to get the game with an Early Access discount! Thank you again for playing my game, and happy holidays!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Chapter 7 Update 3
notes.content:
There’s a lot that still needs to be done, so only a quick update this time. 

I took a break from script writing to add in what I already wrote and tested the events up to what I have finished. Here’s a sneak peek at what’s in store: The bunnoid homeworld Moki!

https://i.imgur.com/3XAdhbp.jpeg

All that's left are the final cutscenes and the post-game area and the dialogues related to those, which have already been planned out. There’s still a lot there to wrap up, so I expect there’d be a lot more writing ahead for me.

That’s it for this time. Barring any major event, I plan on releasing Chapter 7 mid-December at the latest, so look forward to that!

Cheers,
ShenTzu

notes.title: Chapter 7 Update 2
notes.content:
Time for another update! Sorry this one’s a bit late, I was caught up in writing and it completely slipped my mind.

Speaking of which... I’d say the script is about 2/3s done? I’ve written about 14k words so far, and I’m honestly not sure how much more there will be. Chapter 7 is the finale so there’s a lot to wrap up, including all the variations based on your actions throughout the game as well as the different endings. The main thing I want to ensure is that the endings are satisfying, and I will be working towards that. It just might take a while.

In the meantime, new characters!

https://i.imgur.com/MYHmddY.jpeg

The bunnoids aren’t the only one improving their weapons/armour tech, the GFE has some new toys too! Though depending on how things go... they might not be only pointed at the bunnoids.

That’s it for this update! I will try and finish the chapter by mid-late November, but will take the extra time for a satisfying ending if I feel the need to. Either way, look forward to another announcement then!

Cheers,
ShenTzu

notes.title: Chapter 7 Update 1
notes.content:
Wow, it’s been a month already? Somehow it really doesn’t feel like it. Either way, it’s time for the first Chapter 7 update!

https://i.imgur.com/P1m6DLA.jpeg

Planning is complete, and I’ve gotten started on making maps for the chapter, including the one above. That is Protentum Station, a secret Galactic Fuchian Empire research facility and where the majority of Chapter 7 will take place. I can’t say too much about what’s being studied there due to spoilers, but if you’ve been paying attention in previous chapters, you might have a good idea already!

There is one more thing I’d like to bring up. As you may or may not know, Unity recently announced a new “Runtime fee”, where developers using the Unity game engine will have to pay a $0.20 fee PER INSTALL of the game if their game has made $200,000 USD or more in the last 12 months and have at least 200,000 lifetime game installs (those who pay for the Unity Pro and Unity Enterprise subscriptions have a higher threshold and lower fees). Fuchian Chronicles is fortunately unaffected as it is built using RPGMaker MV, but as a fellow indie game developer, I cannot stay quiet about this egregious move by the higher ups at Unity (who allegedly sold their shares in the company prior to the announcement). 

As this is a developing story, details may change and Unity may even walk back this new policy entirely. However, the fact remains that they have shown that they prioritize profits to the point of nickel and diming small developers, many of whom can’t afford this additional fee. Even if they completely walk back the Runtime fee, there’s no telling if they will try to push it again after the heat dies down. I had been considering switching over to using Unity for my future games after finishing Fuchian Chronicles, but now I’ll be looking elsewhere unless there are drastic changes in Unity policy and leadership.

Thank you for taking the time to read my little rant, I felt it was my responsibility to spread awareness of the issue where I can. That’s it for this update, I’ll see you all next time.

Cheers,
ShenTzu

notes.title: Chapter 6 Now Available!
notes.content:
Thank you very much for waiting, Chapter 6 is now available!

https://i.imgur.com/11CD3a8.jpeg

Chapter 6 returns to where everything began, Z-7421 (called Sotenye by the bunnoids), and enters a new phase of the war… the first steps to peace! It has only been about two years since the war began, but it has taken a terrible toll on both sides. Can the two sides finally end the bloodshed?

While it’s not necessary to understand the story, I do recommend playing the standalone demo before starting the chapter. It’ll give additional context to the chapter’s events, and if you’ve been paying attention, you may notice some things! 

As mentioned before, the game is now mostly feature complete, and the focus will be on completing the story. There were still a handful of changes though, they are as follows:

-	Some items and skills have been rebalanced, such as the damage over time dealt by “Tox Gas”.
-	Some achievements have been renamed for more consistency.
-	Some typos/grammar mistakes were fixed.
-	Enemy HP Gauges have been moved a bit to avoid being hidden. I may adjust them further later.

…And that’s it! Not too many changes this time, other than the new chapter of course. As before, the databank has been reset to account for the new entries. You can always unlock all entries using the Journal (hotkey J) if you’d like, though beware of potential spoilers if you do so before completing the chapter. The price of the game has also been increased to reflect the additional new content.

One final thing, Chapter 7 will be the last chapter of the game. After it’s complete, I plan on giving the entire game a once over, adding new things such as portraits some NPCs and finally adding more CG like I wanted from the start. Once that’s done, the game will be ready to come out of Early Access. If everything goes as planned, it will be fully released early 2024, mainly so I can avoid the busy holiday release schedule.

That’s it for this update! I playtested as much as I can, but if I missed any bugs or issues, please post them in the Steam Community thread or email me at shentzugames@yahoo.com, and I’ll fix them as soon as I can. As always, thank you for playing my game, and I hope you enjoy the new chapter!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Chapter 6 Progress Update 3
notes.content:
Another month, another update! I’m working on the script still, but in the meantime, here’s a new character!

https://i.imgur.com/9e94cVV.jpeg

Her name is Fuchs (as in Fuchian), and if you’ve played the original game, Space Fox Kimi, you’ll know her as Kimi’s party member and GFE’s envoy to Earth in that game. Obviously she has much less screentime now and her role is different, but I liked her character in the past and wanted to give her a minor role at least.

Finally, a little bit of bad news: I’m afraid that the script is taking longer than I would like, mainly because of a newly discovered narrative plothole that needed me to revise certain events in chapter 6. I hope to finish by the end of July, but I’m not entirely confident about that deadline. I will commit to finishing the chapter by mid-August though, so it won’t be delayed further. Thank you for understanding.

That’s it for this time! Barring any critical hotfixes or real life emergencies, the next announcement will be the release of chapter 6. See you then!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Chapter 6 Progress Update 2
notes.content:
Has it been another month already? Time sure is going faster than I anticipated… Well, time for another updated! This one's a little early, but I didn't want to sit on this particular update for reasons that'll be apparent.

The new maps are finished, though if time allows I’d like to expand on one of the areas. For now I’m working on the script, which is where the bulk of the work will be for this chapter. There’s a lot going on following the events of Chapter 5! Speaking of which...

https://i.imgur.com/U2bpLen.png

Chapter 6 will have the first meaningful interactions with the bunnoids… and a bunnoid party member! I won’t reveal the circumstances of her joining since it’s a major plot point, but I hope you look forward to it!

Finally, a small update with pretty a pretty big impact: a difficulty setting! I originally designed the game to avoid having overly simple combat that can be won by spamming the regular attack, but now I realize I may have gone too far and made the game frustratingly hard at places. My apologies for that. There is now a difficulty setting in the options menu that ranges from “Story Mode” for players who want to focus on enjoying the story, and “Challenge” difficulty for those who like… well, a challenge. Please be warned that the “Challenge” difficulty may not be balanced, and may even make some encounters outright impossible. You can change the difficulty at any time, so if you do get stuck feel free to lower the difficulty to get past those encounters. This update is now live for both the base game and the demo as of this announcement. Speaking of which, now would be a good time to play the demo if you haven’t already (hint hint). It contains a side story that doesn’t show up in the main game after all! I don't think it would and didn't find any issues while testing, but if this update broke anything please let me know and I'll fix it asap.

That’s it for this update! At this point I’m a little hesitant to promise that Chapter 6 will be released in a month, but I’ll certainly do my best to meet this goal. Either way, you can look forward to another announcement then, and more frequent updates on my Twitter @ShenTzuGames! Thank you as always for your continued support!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Chapter 5 Hotfix
notes.content: Fixed a bug where your strike craft weren't added back in for the start of chapter 5 if they were destroyed in a previous chapter. Thanks to Screethegargoyle for pointing this out!

notes.title: Chapter 6 Progress Update 1
notes.content:
Another month, another update, hope everyone’s doing well! Some unexpected business took me away from work for a wwhile, but I was able finish planning out Chapter 6. I can’t share much about it because spoilers, but I do have this for you!
https://i.imgur.com/MviSvy2.jpeg
If the setting looks familiar, it should! Chapter 6 goes back to where it all began, Z-7421, or as the bunnoids call it, Sotenye! After the events of Chapter 5, the GFE can finally properly communicate with the bunnoids and learn more about the enemy they’ve been fighting for so long, and maybe even broker a ceasefire. Perhaps with understanding, there can finally be peace?

That’s it for this update! I understand it’s a short one, but I haven’t had the time to work on that much on the game this past month. I promise the next update will have more, especially in the graphics department. Until then, thank you for your continued support! 

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Chapter 5 Now Available!
notes.content:
Hope everyone’s doing well, I come bearing news: Chapter 5 has now been released! 

https://i.imgur.com/cGckG0T.jpeg

The tides of war turn against the Fuchians as the bunnoids conduct a daring attack on Fleet Eternity. Kimi rushes to join her fleet mates in defence of her home, but will it be enough?

My apologies for not making an update post earlier like I usually would. Between taking on commissions and job hunting, this has been a hectic month for me so far. Things have calmed down enough for me to finish the chapter though, so here we are! In addition to the chapter release, some other changes have been made to the game. They are as follows:

-	Updated AI for enemy and allied ships. They are now smarter and won’t do illogical things such as using anti-strikecraft skills when there aren’t any strike craft on the field as much.
-	Anti-strikecraft skills such as flak shot and flak burst now cost more TP, but accumulated TP now carries between battles so you no longer have to charge it up at the start of battles. This also just makes more sense in my opinion. It’s not like you’d unload the AA guns between battles after all.
-	Strikecraft can now use the "Paint Target" skill for additional utility. If they don't already know it, they'll learn it at the start of Chapter 5.
-	Yna’s Rescue skill (used in Chapter 4) has been nerfed a bit with a lower success rate.
-	Unachieved achievements icons have been turned into something more generic to help avoid spoilers.
-	The game now autosaves in certain locations throughout the game in addition to autosaving normally. This mainly occurs when completing sections in a chapter, and is aimed at preventing lost progress in case of crashes or something after boss fights.

As before, the encyclopedia will be reset upon starting the chapter to accommodate the new entries, and you can unlock all entries using the debug menu in the journal (shortcut J). The price of the game has also been increased to reflect the new content.

That’s it for this update! As always, please post any bugs you come across in the Steam Community thread, or email me at shentzugames@yahoo.com, and I’ll fix them as soon as I can. Thank you for playing my game, and I hope you enjoy the new chapter!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Chapter 5 Update 1
notes.content:
Hello everyone! It’s been about a month and so it’s time for an update!

https://static.wixstatic.com/media/e4c1c1_47b1a401deb54f86abffb036a712b08c~mv2.gif

Chapter five is about halfway done, and the way things are looking, will be finished in early to mid-April. Due to the prevalence of space battles in this chapter, I improved the AI of enemy and allied spacecraft so they don't do stupid things such as using anti fighter skills against capital ships as much. This will also apply to previous space battles, but the updated AI won’t be released until Chapter 5 is finished.

As for what’s in the second half of Chapter 5… It’s been planned out but I don’t have much to show from it yet. So here’s a sneak peak at a new enemy that you’ll encounter!

https://i.imgur.com/EhU9kbU.png

That’s it for this update, though before I sign off I’d like to get your opinion on something. What would you like to see in these update posts? Feature/mechanics wise I think the game is more or less complete, so I’ll be more focused on finishing the story and adding related locale, characters, enemies, and new equipment. Obviously I won’t be able to show everything due to spoilers, but which of the new stuff would you like to see most? Let me know and I’ll take it into consideration for the next update!

Thank you for your continued support, and look forward to the release of Chapter 5!
- ShenTzu

https://i.imgur.com/7CbOo50.jpeg

Chapter 5 will feature the battle of Eternity’s Dawn, where the bunnoids attack with a massive armada. It will be the largest and most dangerous battle of the war so far, but Kimi will do her part to defend her home.

notes.title: Chapter 4 Progress Update 2
notes.content:
Month two of developing Chapter 4! All the new maps have been finished, and so I’ve moved onto writing the script. 

https://i.imgur.com/XyB1ovt.gif

And that’s it! See you next time!

…I jest, but the truth is I’ve had to take on a few side jobs to help pay the bills, so progress this month has been slower than I would like (did you know I did the maps for Sierra Lee’s Once Ever After, and a few maps for her other game, The Last Sovereign?). At this point I can’t say for sure if this will lead to a delay to the planned release of Chapter 4 in a month or so, but wanted to give you guys a heads up in case there is. I’d also like to take this opportunity to reassure you guys that I will finish the game even if I need to take a full time job to pay bills, though if it does come to that, each chapter will likely take much longer to release.

Now that’s out of the way, let’s get back to Chapter 4.

Right now I don’t plan on adding any new major features/mechanics for this chapter, mainly to reduce the odds of additional delays. There will still be new items, enemies, and equipment of course, just no new brand new mechanics like how I added weapon proficiency and equipment modding in Chapter 3. I do have a few other ideas I’d like to implement, but those are mainly on the backburner… except one.

The Demo!

I know the importance of demos for games, but decided against making one since I felt it was unfair to have one while only one or two chapters were released as paid content. This is why I’m only making a demo once Chapter 4 is released. Yes, making a demo, as in it’ll be new content. I already roughly mapped out how it’ll go and just need to work out a few kinks and plot consistencies to make sure it ties in well with established events. Based on my plans, it probably won’t be as long as a full chapter, but should fill in a bit of the story that I couldn’t fit in before.

That’s it for this update! Hope you look forward to the release!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Minor Update - New Savings Features and Fixed Playtime Tracking
notes.content:
-	Updated saving system. Autosaves now have a dedicated save slot which cannot be manually saved into, thanks to CloudyCloudcloud for the suggestion! While I was at it, I also added quicksaving/quickloading to the game (which also comes with its own dedicated save slot). Press F5 to quicksave and F9 to quickload. Of course, you still won’t be able to quicksave/load when saving/loading is disabled.
-	Fixed playtime tracking. Apparently the way playtime was being tracked was dependent on your computer/monitor’s FPS, meaning that you could have a drastically different playtime than reality. That’s been fixed now, and the playtime should reflect real time. Don’t worry if you see play time as “Na : Na : Na”, it’ll go back to normal when you next make a save. It does reset the time to “00 : 00 : 00” though, thank you for understanding. There’s also an option in the debug menu to reset the playtime in case the timer does not fix itself, or if you want to reset it for any reason. Thanks to Screethegargoyle for catching this!
-	Did you know that taking a shower (either at home or in the crew bathrooms) actually gives you a minor buff to agility and evasion for the chapter? Well now you do! And now when you take a shower, you’ll be notified about the buff.
-	Fixed a few instances where the incorrect portrait was shown in Chapter 3.

notes.title: Chapter 4 Progress Update 1
notes.content:
It’s been about a month since Chapter 3 was released, and it’s been a busy one. Chapter 4 has been planned out and I’ve been working on new maps for it, here’s a sneak peek at some of the new content!

https://i.imgur.com/3k7dMZo.jpeg

https://i.imgur.com/SuUFS8y.jpeg

You might think that the aesthetic looks familiar, and you’d be right. Chapter 4 has Kimi and Jeanne returning to Gliese Delta, the primitive planet they went to for training back in Chapter 1. A lot has changed in the months since then. They graduated from the academy, war with the bunnoids broke out, and Gliese Delta itself was formally annexed into the Empire. So what’s going on here? You’ll have to find out when the chapter is released! You might even see some familiar faces, if you did a certain thing way back when.

Chapter 4 also marks the first major departure from the original game, Space Fox Kimi, and I expect there to be more deviations in future chapters. I’m also planning on making a demo for the game now that a few chapters have been released. It will have new content/story that’s not part of the main game, but I’m still working out the details so I’ll leave it at that for now.

Follow me on Twitter @ShenTzuGames for more frequent updates, and as always, thank you for playing my game and for helping me with bug reporting and suggestions! I hope you enjoyed the game so far, and hope you’ll look forward to Chapter 4!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Chapter 3 of Fuchian Chronicles released!
notes.content:
Thank you for waiting everyone! As of this post, Chapter 3 of Fuchian Chronicles is now live! Kimi has more or less gotten used to life on the Canis now, but little does she know, everything is about to change for her. Meanwhile, her parents Ava and Rocco are deployed as part of the Fuchians first counter offensive against the bunnoids. Is this where the tide of war turns?

In addition to new story content, many new gameplay features have been added! See below for details.


 New Feature: In Game Encyclopedia. An in-game encyclopedia has been added to the game, documenting all the enemies, items, equipment, skills, and states. You can find it by using the Journal item (or pressing “J” in the field) and selecting “Open Databank”, or simply pressing “E” in the field. Lore such as the history of the Empire (which has been expanded) has been moved into the encyclopedia as well, along with new lore entries describing the ships of the Empire. Likewise the tutorials can now be found in the encyclopedia. These entries can be unlocked via gameplay/exploration.

Due to the evolving nature of the game, it may be necessary to reset encyclopedia progress as new enemies, items, lore, etc are added to the game. As such, I’ve added a new debug menu in the Journal, and included an option there to unlock all encyclopedia entries for those who would like to use it. This function will be removed once the game is finished.

 New Feature: Item Disassembly. For an item called the “Reassembler”, not being able to break down un-needed items into raw materials didn’t really make sense. But that changes now! To disassemble items, go into the item menu and select the item (like you were going to use it), and select “disassemble” where you can see what materials you can get from it. Most items can be disassembled, but keep in mind you won’t get more materials than it costs to make them (the ones that can be crafted at least). More equipment disassembly will likely be added later.

 New Feature: Weapon Proficiency. Characters will now become more proficient with specific weapon types (rifles, pistols, melee weapons, etc) the more they use it. Proficiency experience is gained every time they attack with the weapon, and each level in proficiency increases their accuracy and critical hit rate with the weapon type a little. 

 New Feature: Equipment Modification. Most pieces of equipment can now be customized using various pieces of augments. These range from changing the equipment’s stats to adding status effects, to adding new skills. Basic augments can be crafted the same way you craft supplies and bought from the store starting in Ch2, while some special augments can be earned by helping people and occasionally dropped by enemies. Generally, the further in the story you are, the more augments you can craft/buy, and more will be added in future chapters.

 Updated Crafting Menu. Instead of the jury-rigged crafting menu that’s been in use so far, there is now a proper crafting menu! You can now make multiple items at once, and you won’t be kicked out of the menu after making something. Use the Reassembler item to enter the crafting menu, or press the R key in the field, just as before.

 Updated drop table. After rewatching an old Extra Credits video, I realized that only getting crafting materials from combat is not exactly satisfying. As such, enemy drops have been tweaked a bit to include additional drops, especially the bosses. You can now get supplies and even some equipment from enemies, and of course, unwanted items can be disassembled into crafting materials.

 Updated how portraits appear. Multiple portraits can now show up at the same time and can also move to make cutscenes more dynamic.

As mentioned in my previous news update, some of these features are unfortunately incompatible with existing saves, so you will need to start a new game. Thank you for understanding. To make up for this, I’ve added an item to help you get back to where you left off more easily: the OP Grenade of OPness. It is a lore breaking grenade that will kill all enemies on screen, including bosses, and completely trivializes all fights. You will still get item and equipment drops as normal, but you will lose out on weapon proficiency gains by doing so. To get this item, go to the debug menu in the Journal and select “OP Grenade”. Doing so will also grant you the item for use in space battles, aside from a certain one in Chapter 2. The grenade will be taken away once you start Chapter 3.

A few more quality of life changes have also been added, along with a few other balances, tweaks, and fixes. Details are as follows:


 More hotkeys added. Pressing “I” now opens the inventory, “K” opens the Skills menu, “E” opens the Databank, and “M” now toggles the amount of materials you have (if you have a Reassembler).
 Added a visual indicator when characters gain experience so you can see how far you are to the next “Level up”.
 Some ships have been renamed to better fit with the rest of the GFE’s naming conventions. The Maho Tahu is now the Arctos, the Atsuage is now the Savini, and the Agedashi is now the Vinae.
 Gameover screen now allows you to load a save directly instead of needing to return to the main menu first.
 Prices of various items have been rebalanced to better fit with their crafting material cost/material gains from disassembling them. In general, it will not cost you more to buy an item than it does to buy the crafting materials required to craft the same item. At the same time, the value of materials you can get from disassembling the item will not be more than if you were to sell the item directly.
 Some enemies, equipment, and characters have been rebalanced, including the specialist in Chapter 1 and the dropship in Chapter 2.
 Full screen now functions properly. Press F4 to toggle full screen.

As before, please let me know if you find any bugs, or if you have any suggestions! The price of the game has also been increased to reflect the new content available. Once again, thank you for playing my game, and I hope you enjoy Chapter 3!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Chapter 3 Update 3
notes.content:
Just a quick update this time, though with some important news. 

The good news is, Chapter 3 is finished! I’m just waiting on some art, and while I’m doing that I’m adding a few more features to the game. Which brings me to the other bit of news.

Thus far I’ve tried my best to add fixes to get around the need to restart the game when new features are added, but unfortunately there’s finally a new feature that I’d like to add that is incompatible with existing saves. That feature is weapon proficiency, making the character more effective using a type of weapon the more they use it. I’ve been trying to find ways to add more incentive to fighting, and think this would be a good way to do so in addition to the other stuff. 

https://i.imgur.com/n3NJFmV.png

As mentioned before, this new feature unfortunately does require a new save. I thank you for understanding, and will try to add something to make it easier for players who have already played before to get back to where they left off. I’ll also try my best to avoid adding features that require restarts, but can’t promise that it won’t happen again, especially if the new feature would significantly improve the game.

On the bright side, you’ll be able to see the changes in the cutscenes that resulted from the new portrait system, so I hope you’ll enjoy that.

And since there will be a restart, I’m taking the opportunity to add additional features. I won’t reveal what those features are just yet, mainly because I’m still testing them. Based on the current state of things, I’m estimating that Chapter 3, along with all the new features, will be released at the end of July. Look forward to it!

notes.title: Chapter 3 Progress Update 2
notes.content:
Has it been another month already? Geez times goes by so fast. Time for another update!

The maps and script for Chapter 3 are finished, all that’s left is to add the events in and test things! Before I can do that however, I need rework a lot of the cutscenes and interactions in Chapters 1 and 2. Why? Because I’m making the portraits/busts much more dynamic!
[previewyoutube=EQO4qMlea7Q;full][/previewyoutube]
As you can see, portraits can now alongside each other, and can also move to better convey the action taking place. I was debating about whether to implement this now, or focus on releasing Chapter 3 first, but ultimately decided that it was better to do this now since the longer I wait to add this feature, the more I would have to redo. Hopefully this won’t delay Chapter 3’s release too much, but if there are any delays, I thank you for your understanding and hope you will agree that this addition is worth it.

I mentioned in my previous progress update that I was adding/reworking other features as well. In addition to the Databank, another important feature that’s being updated is the crafting menu. You will be able to craft multiple items at once, and will no longer be kicked out of the menu after crafting a single item. More importantly, you will also be able to disassemble items into raw materials!

https://i.imgur.com/WIxfFxh.png

Considering the item used in crafting is called the “Reassembler”, it didn’t make much sense to not be able to break down unwanted items into more useful materials. But now you can! You will be able to disassemble just about any consumable, and even some trophies, in a pinch.

As always, follow me on Twitter @ShenTzuGames for more frequent updates. If everything goes according to plan, this should be the last progress update before the release of Chapter 3. Either way, I’ll make another post in about a month. See you then!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Chapter 3 Progress Update
notes.content:
Hello everyone! It’s been about a month since the release of Chapter 2, and so it’s time for a little update on my progress on Chapter 3.

https://i.imgur.com/3Zv5RcD.jpeg

Thus far the only space based content has been individual battles, but Chapter 3 will introduce the first real space based map! Considering space based exploration is one of the marketed selling points of the game, I’m happy to finally introduce some space exploration. While ground based maps will still be the focus, I plan on having more space maps later on. 

Of course, Chapter 3 will still have ground content.

https://i.imgur.com/K74J4af.jpeg

Chapter 3 will also have the first look at a bunnoid locale. It’ll be the first real chance to learn a bit about the bunnoids and their culture, who have so far been more or less a faceless enemy. What are the bunnoids like? Are they really all machines? Do they all eat carrots? You will finally be able to start answering some of these questions, though the answer to the last one is almost certainly yes.

And finally, I’ve been gradually adding new features and improving on some existing features in the game. One of the major new additions to the game is… the Databank!

https://i.imgur.com/UB0lUPC.png

The journal system I’ve been using, though functional, is rather inelegant and limited. Now there will be a proper in-game encyclopedia, recording enemies, equipment, lore, and more! More encyclopedia entries will be added as the game progresses, and I may add additional categories (such as character profiles) later on. I’m working on other features as well, but I’ll save them for a future blog post.

One last thing: Thank you thus far for the support, including catching bugs I missed and giving suggestions! I posted in the suggestions thread earlier but would like to re-iterate: if you agree with someone else’s suggestion, especially regarding game difficulty, please say so! It would really help me gauge which suggestions would help improve the game the most. 

Once again, thank you for playing my game, and I hope you look forward to Chapter 3!

- ShenTzu

notes.title: Fuchian Chronicles Chapter 2 now available!
notes.content:
Thank you for waiting, as of this post, Chapter 2 of Fuchian Chronicles is now live! Kimi is being deployed on the GFE Canis as war with the bunnoids rages on. What will Kimi encounter on her first proper mission?

If you've played Chapter 1 previously, simply load up your latest save and continue playing from there. And if you'd like a refresher, you can press J in game to open the journal and get a recap of the events and your choices in Chapter 1. You can also review tutorials there to get a refresher of gameplay elements.

Along with the new chapter, many new features have been added to the game. See below for the major changes:

 Autosaving added! By default, autosaves occur every 5 minutes (not including time spent in dialogue/cutscenes/battle), but you can change this in the journal (press J). Autosaves are automatically placed in the first save slot, so please use the remaining slots for manual saves. 
 Mid-battle equipment changing added! Since the skills available to you are based on what you have equipped, this is a feature I wanted to have since the beginning but couldn’t since it broke a few things. But I got it working now! Scroll down the command menu when it’s your turn and you can have the currently active party member change their equipment. You can’t do this consecutively though, so make sure to plan your equipment carefully.

Keep in mind that you can’t change ship equipment mid-battle because that makes no sense.
 Armour Piercing Ammo has been reworked! Instead of giving a percent attack bonus, using this item now adds an Armour piercing “element” to gun attacks, which does more damage to armoured enemies. Armoured enemies now have slightly increased defence to compensate, making them more resistant to regular attacks. Which enemies are armoured? Their appearance is a good indicator!
 “Level up” mechanic added! It’s similar to the traditional level up in RPGs in that party members get exp after fighting, and once a threshold is met they gain extra stats. However, the stat gains are minor and meant to reflect Kimi and her fellow soldiers gaining battle experience. Grinding remains optional as promised, and all fights are possible without “leveling up”. I mainly added this mechanic as an extra incentive to fight the optional encounters, and to make story fights a bit easier for those who want it.
 New Achievements! In addition to new achievements relating to Chapter 2, there are now achievements relating to how many NPCs you help around the ship and how many battles you’ve fought in. You don’t need to help all the NPCs to earn the achievement, but you will need to help more NPCs than there are available in Chapter 2. 

If you’re loading from the end of Chapter 1, you can talk to Nina (the gray haired cafeteria lady in the Mess Hall) twice after the opening cutscene to update the total number of people you’ve helped. Nina will also let you gain some extra stats to make up for the “level ups” you may have missed when fighting enemies in Chapter 1, and doing so will add 10 to your progress for the “Diligent Cadet” and “Veteran Soldier” achievements.  This feature will be removed once the game is complete.

Several minor tweaks and features have been added as well:

 New items/equipment/skills menus for more functionality, primarily to prevent use of incompatible items/skills. This means that you can't accidentally waste ammo items by using them on characters that don't have guns equipped anymore! As a result, ammo items can no longer be used out of battle, but to make up for that, using them in battle no longer uses up your turn. The “Deploy Strikecraft” skill no longer consumes the actor’s turn as well.
 Message backlog feature added. Press “Page Up” during dialogue to see the backlog.
 Updated options menu with more settings such as FPS sync and message speed. If the game suddenly seems to be running in slow motion and/or if your monitor runs at over 60FPS, please turn FPS sync on.
 Save screen updated to show what chapter you’re in. Don’t worry if you see a 0 above your location in the save file, it’ll be updated to show the current chapter upon changing to a new chapter.
 Shift key now toggles between running and walking instead of needing to hold it down when the “Always Run” option is enabled. 
 Minor changes to dialogue to make the speech more “foxy” with some new expressions.

As before, I playtested this as much as I could, but may have missed a few things. If you see any bugs/typos/errors/etc please post it the relevant thread in the Community Hub, same with suggestions. I avoid posting in the suggestions thread as to not influence discussion, but rest assured that I do read it!

Finally, the price of the game has been increased as I said it would in the Early Access notes. The price will continue to increase every time a new chapter is released, but you'll get access to all chapters of the game regardless of when you bought it. This means that those who buy the game early in development will effectively get the game at a steep discount. It's my way of thanking people for supporting me during development.

Thank you again for playing my game! I hope you enjoy Chapter 2, and future chapters as well!

- ShenTzu
